newsitem.title: FRANCE: Immigrants stage fresh protest in France.
newsitem.headline: Immigrants stage fresh protest in France.

text.p: Two African immigrants, who were among some 220 ejected from a Paris church last summer, have begun a hunger strike in a fresh protest to demand residency rights, the group's spokesman Abubakr Diop said on Friday.
Diop said the two, a 44-year-old woman from Senegal who has been living in France for 19 years, and a man from Mali, began fasting on Christmas Day together with a French supporter of Polish descent.

Diop said other protesters would demonstrate every week, starting next Thursday, outside President Jacques Chirac's Elysee palace to denounce what they call bad faith on the part of the government in negotiations on their legal status.
The immigrants have staged sporadic protests since police last August ejected them from Saint-Bernard church in Paris, where they were staging a sit-in.
Diop said the government had since deported 13 and promised residence permits to 101, while the situation of the others remained unresolved.
Many immigrants say they once enjoyed residence rights but were pushed into illegality when laws were stiffened in 1993 to curb immigration.
The government has said they have no legal right to stay in France but their cases will be reviewed individually on humanitarian grounds.
